NEW PODCAST: ARRI Goes Small, Sony Goes Big: HONOR’s ARRI Phone & Sony RIALTO 65 – Focus Check ep141 →🎙️ WATCH/LISTEN Now
Watch/Listen Now ARRI Goes Small, Sony Goes Big: HONOR’s ARRI Phone & Sony RIALTO 65 🎙️NEW PODCAST
Adobe has released Premiere 27.0 with Color Mode, an AI Assistant panel, and tools that generate music, sound effects, and soundscapes in the timeline.
The update also retires the Lumetri Color panel, ends support for Intel Macs, and makes the AI Assistant draw Firefly credits with no cost estimate before a prompt runs.
The release arrives during Adobe MAX in Miami Beach.
Adobe lists the changes in the Premiere 27.0 release post .
Several of the features were in public beta since spring, and we covered the Color Mode beta when Adobe first showed it.
Color Mode is a dedicated grading workspace behind a new Color tab next to Edit.

Adobe describes it as “a dedicated color-grading workspace designed to help you correct individual shots, create consistent looks, and manage color across an entire sequence.” It has a Clip Grid, three operation types (Adjust, Style, and LUT), and grades that apply to a clip, a group, or the complete sequence.
A new HSL Masking tool isolates areas by hue, saturation, and luminance and combines with other masks.
The larger change is what goes away.

In the Color Mode post , Adobe writes that “the Lumetri Color panel is being retired in Premiere 27.0,” while the Lumetri Color effect stays available and existing grades remain adjustable in Effect Controls.
Adobe recommends that editors who are finishing a Lumetri-heavy project complete it in Premiere 26.x first.
The company also notes that 8K media can have performance problems in an 8K sequence.
The first user replies under that post are about speed for small jobs.

One editor objects that a fast exposure or white balance correction now needs the Color tab or a Lumetri effect on each clip, and another reports that the controls are too sensitive with a pen tablet.
The AI Assistant panel reads the project and does editing tasks from plain-language requests.
During the beta that started in June, Adobe gave users free daily credits for it.

In a separate post , community manager Matt Christensen writes that Adobe is “removing the daily and weekly limits on usage” and that “the Assistant will use Firefly credits from your Adobe account’s plan.”
Each response shows the credits it used after the fact.

When a user asked if the cost is visible before a request runs, Matt answered: “No, it’s not possible to estimate the amount of credits that will be used when working with the Assistant.” He added that the number depends on the sequence and on the tools the Assistant needs.
Adobe’s own example in that post gives a sense of scale.
A request to cut an interview down to the first answer to each question shortened a sequence from 4:43 to about 1:56 and used 19.83 credits.
According to Adobe’s generative credits FAQ , Creative Cloud Pro includes 4,000 monthly credits, while Creative Cloud Standard and single-app plans bought since June 17, 2025 include 25.
On those plans, this one request is about four fifths of the monthly allowance, and credits do not roll over.
Blackmagic Design took a different route in DaVinci Resolve 21.1 , which connects to external AI assistants through MCP and leaves the choice and the cost of the model to the user.
The Generative Media Tool now creates images, music, and soundscapes in addition to video and sound effects.
The editor selects a region in the timeline, types a prompt, and the result goes into the sequence.
Generate Music makes instrumental tracks only.
Generate Soundscape analyzes the picture and builds ambience and effect layers as a starting point.
Generative Extend can now create the missing frames when a clip is too short for a transition.
Unlike the Assistant, these tools show an estimated credit cost before they run.

Adobe states that prompts, media, and reference frames “aren’t used to train Adobe or partner AI models.” For partner models, the user is responsible for deciding if the output is appropriate for a project, and some partner models are not available on business plans.
The 27.0 posts do not name the partner models.
For the previous version, Adobe listed Google Veo, Kling, Runway, and Luma.
Separate Crosstalk splits overlapping speakers into separate stems.
Auto Ducking now updates its keyframes when clips are added, trimmed, or muted.

The Speed/Duration dialog has new audio stretching modes and pitch controls, so a retimed clip does not need a trip to Audition. iXML metadata shows on audio clips in the timeline and Source Monitor, and waveforms draw in real time during recording.
The Effects panel has animated thumbnails and a Preview from Source function.
Effects and masks appear as collapsible cards in the Properties panel, Object Mask tracks better, and there are eight new effects, among them Radial Blur and Zoom Blur.
Premiere 27.0 needs Windows 11 version 24H2 or later, or an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 15 or later.
Intel Macs stay on version 26.x.
On Windows, Premiere does not start without a supported GPU.
Adobe has also said that version 28.0 will not install on any Windows 10 system.
The release adds native Windows on ARM support for systems with the NVIDIA RTX Spark chip, which we reported on in June .
